about: Leads for Seia (Serra da Estrela), started from a reader tip on r/Lisbon, 2026-10-22.

leads.name: The Chestnuts of Souto da Lapa
leads.place: Souto da Lapa, Lapa dos Dinheiros, Seia, Serra da Estrela
leads.source: reader tip on r/Lisbon, 2026-10-22 (no name kept): 'castanheiros centenários e milenares de troncos gigantescos e cavidades impressionantes', one that eight people could not reach around; coordinates are the village, not a trunk
leads.note: A grove, so the collectible point is the one trunk worth the walk (the eight-person chestnut). Needs: which tree, its position, a source for its age (the Seia municipality or ICNF; the ICNF register has only the Solar de Santa Rita yew for this parish), and an open-licence photograph. The tipster posted a photo of one trunk in the thread (reddit.com/r/Lisbon/comments/1xci4vn/comment/19ri7whjaowhu), but said on 2026-10-23 their photos there were taken from the internet: not theirs, not usable; at most a pointer to which trunk. Day trip from Seia; not a Lisbon tree. Research 2026-10-23: komoot's Seia natural-monuments guide (user content, facts only) places 'Lapa Souto' south of the village by the Caniça river beach (beach at about 40.3853, -7.6973) and calls the trees centuries-old, no trunk named. Commons has nothing of the grove: a geosearch within 4 km brings up the river beach, the falls and the village, but no chestnut. The ICNF register has no chestnut here. No web source names the big trunk. Not to be confused with 'Soutos da Lapa', the protected-origin chestnut region around Sernancelhe and Penedono. Next angle: the Seia municipality or the Serra da Estrela Geopark, a Caniça walking route, or a reader in the app.
